author: Detlef Vollmann

evidence.note: The revision-history section of P0260R20 records what changed from P0260R19 (2025-06-18): the author added more rationale, made the concepts non-exposition-only as decided by SG1 in Brno, and fixed typos. Separately it records that from P0260R18 to P0260R19 the author renamed std::conqueue_errc to std::conqueue_status as decided by LEWG in Sofia.
evidence.title: P0260R19 C++ Concurrent Queues
evidence.what_changed: From P0260R19 to P0260R20 the author added more rationale and made the concepts non-exposition-only per SG1's Brno decision; from P0260R18 to P0260R19 the author renamed std::conqueue_errc to std::conqueue_status as decided by LEWG in Sofia. These are concessions to committee direction, while the core proposal (concurrent queue concepts plus bounded_queue and blocking/non-blocking/async operations) persisted.

evidence.note: LEWG minutes from Varna 2023-06-15, pasted into the WG21 papers tracking issue, record Detlef Vollmann as champion of P0260. Two polls on re-adding is_empty/is_full queries failed with no consensus, and LEWG directed the author to explore a system_error-derived exception type, try_push interfaces preventing data loss, noexcept-movable element types, and type erasure in the next revision.
evidence.title: LEWG Varna 2023-06-15 minutes as pasted in cplusplus/papers issue #99

evidence.note: SG1 minutes from Issaquah 2023-02-07, pasted in the cplusplus/papers issue, show SG1 declined to retake its earlier unanimous-consent decision that the P0260R5 design (authored by Crowl, Mysen, and Vollmann) was appropriate for a concurrency TS, and a temperature poll to forward the design to LEWG for C++26 failed (3 SF / 7 F / 6 N / 2 A / 3 SA); stated opposition worried that blocking operations and async APIs hiding implementation would not fit senders/receivers.
evidence.title: SG1 Issaquah 2023-02-07 minutes as pasted in cplusplus/papers issue #99

position: Detlef Vollmann is a named author of P0260 and has championed the proposal in WG21, so his documented position favors standardizing concurrent queue concepts (basic_concurrent_queue, concurrent_queue, async_concurrent_queue) and a concrete std::bounded_queue with blocking, try_*, and async_* operations. Across revisions he accepted committee-directed changes—renaming conqueue_errc to conqueue_status per LEWG in Sofia, making the concepts non-exposition-only per SG1 in Brno, and earlier splitting one concept into three and requiring lockfree try_* operations after SG1 feedback—while keeping the core design. In the Issaquah 2023 SG1 discussion his P0260R5 design was confirmed appropriate for a concurrency TS but a poll to forward it to LEWG for C++26 failed (3 SF / 7 F / 6 N / 2 A / 3 SA) over blocking operations and sender/receiver integration, and he continued pursuing the direction. As champion at LEWG Varna 2023 he argued for re-adding is_empty/is_full queries, which failed with no consensus, and was directed to explore a system_error-derived exception type, data-loss-free try_push interfaces, noexcept-movable element types, and type erasure.
recommendation: Proposes standardizing concurrent queue concepts (basic_concurrent_queue, concurrent_queue, async_concurrent_queue) and a concrete std::bounded_queue class, along with a conqueue_status enum and blocking, non-blocking try_*, and asynchronous async_* push/pop operations.
title: C++ Concurrent Queues
